pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (page labels 16% off); 14-day Pro trial, no card; 30-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra users, workspaces and profiles are paid add-ons with prices shown only inside the app; profile caps count every connected account; temporary promo codes are excluded.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For SocialBee, organize posts into evergreen categories and schedule them across networks. The hard boundary is many connectors, content recycling, concierge services, and team workflow, plus api access, connector upkeep, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Draft posts, organize them into evergreen categories, schedule them across networks, preview them accurately, publish through official APIs, and retain a searchable content calendar.
requirements: developer application for one social network
whatYouLose: many connectors, content recycling, concierge services, and team workflow
moatNotes: API access, connector upkeep, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for SocialBee because the scheduler is easy; staying approved and correct across constantly changing social APIs is the subscription. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, API policy changes, media limits, queues, retries, rate limits, webhooks, tokens, and moderation workflows, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Active open-source social media scheduling platform.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: Reusable schedules and broad publishing with analytics; evergreen categories are less explicit, but the loop works.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or clone the repository and deploy with Docker Compose or a supported PaaS.
facts.engines: No model is bundled; its REST API and MCP server connect external agents such as Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor or custom clients.
facts.dataFormat: Hosted data lives in BrightBean's cloud; self-hosted data uses PostgreSQL 16+ with media on local disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: BrightBean can repeat schedules, but it lacks SocialBee's explicit category-based evergreen library and category-level controls.
facts.setupBlocker: Connecting social networks requires first-party platform developer/OAuth credentials; self-hosting also requires Docker or a PaaS.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: Queues are the product: fill categories, set times and let old posts circulate again.

facts.install: Docker Compose is recommended; a manual Laravel/Composer installation is also documented.
facts.dataFormat: MySQL stores application data, Redis handles queues/cache, and media uses local/public disk or S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost's queues are useful, but the Lite edition lacks SocialBee's team, analytics and AI-assisted category-management depth.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a server with Docker plus social-platform app credentials; the manual path also needs PHP, Composer, Supervisor, cron, Redis and FFmpeg.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: Recurring posts and multi-network scheduling replace the evergreen loop; self-hosting is the new category.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting.
facts.engines: Optional AI/media features connect to OpenAI, ElevenLabs, fal.ai, Tavily, KieAI and Transloadit.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL holds application data; Redis and Temporal support jobs; media is stored locally or in Cloudflare R2/S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Recurring posts are less category-native than SocialBee's evergreen system, and Postiz also requires self-hosted operations.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is straightforward; self-hosting requires Docker, social OAuth apps, and a PostgreSQL, Redis and Temporal stack.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Accelerate plan and a single-network scheduler DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for SocialBee in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one official social-platform API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: draft posts, organize them into evergreen categories, schedule them across networks, preview them accurately, publish through official APIs, and retain a searchable content calendar.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support drafts, scheduled times, queues, campaigns, tags, and a weekly calendar.
Connect exactly one social network using its documented OAuth flow.
Validate character, media, aspect-ratio, and file-size limits before scheduling.
Publish through an idempotent background job with retries and clear failure states.
Store platform post identifiers and refresh publication status without scraping.
Add reusable snippets, local media storage, CSV export, and a token reconnect flow.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out unofficial automation or scraping.
Deliberately leave out multi-network inbox and social listening.
Deliberately leave out agency approvals, white labelling, and enterprise reporting.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
